title: White Rice with Dark Green Vegetables and Tomatoes/Tomato Sauce, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of boiled white rice, dark green vegetables (such as broccoli, spinach or green beans) and tomatoes or a tomato‑based sauce. A small amount of fat is added to enhance flavor and aid the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is a staple carbohydrate source for many cultures worldwide.
Dark green vegetables are rich in chlorophyll, giving them their characteristic color and antioxidant properties.
Tomatoes contain lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.
Adding a modest amount of fat improves the bioavailability of carotenoids and vitamin A from tomatoes.
The dish can be easily adapted to different cuisines by changing the type of sauce or spices.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice provides a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbohydrates.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice supplies thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Tomatoes and dark green vegetables deliver vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, and lycopene, contributing to cellular protection.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables promotes intestinal motility and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Improved nutrient absorption
items.content: The added fat helps the body absorb fat‑soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K more efficiently.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can cause a rapid rise in blood glucose; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Fat intolerance
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to certain fats (e.g., butter).

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the sauce is prepared with added salt, the dish may become a source of excess sodium.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Dark green vegetables can carry pesticide residues; thorough washing or choosing organic produce is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a side or a main course. You can garnish with herbs, spices, or add a protein source such as chicken, tofu, or fish. Use tomato sauce instead of fresh tomatoes if preferred.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When reheating, add a splash of water or broth to restore moisture.
